name: U.S. Climate Reference Network (USCRN)
description: The U.S. Climate Reference Network (USCRN) is a precision climate monitoring network of 114 stations across the contiguous United States (plus supplemental stations in Alaska and Hawaii) designed by NOAA NCEI to monitor national climate trends with pristine accuracy. Stations are sited in open, rural environments away from artificial heat islands and equipped with triple-redundant sensors measuring air temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, surface temperature, wind speed, relative humidity, and soil moisture/temperature at multiple depths.
